statistical inference procedures for bivariate Archimedean copulas in the presence of censored data.
the problem of selecting a bivariate distribution function from an Archimedean class of copula models.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although the Archimedean copulas are a very useful tool for modelling dependence structures in a variety of applications, the statistical inference procedures for these models are not yet well developed.
the proposed method is a useful alternative for the construction of bivariate copulas, especially when the sample size is small.
the semiparametric approach to estimating an Archimedean dependence structure is not only feasible but also quite efficient, as it is shown by the Monte Carlo simulation results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the semiparametric procedure is a useful alternative to the usual maximum likelihood approach, which requires knowledge of the marginals, and that it provides an easy way of testing the hypothesis that the dependence structure of the sample is Archimedean.

we have proposed a general approach to the estimation of bivariate Archimedean copulas that does not rely on any specific parametric form for the marginals and is applicable in the case of right-censored data.

the proposed estimator of the Archimedean copulas is asymptotically normal and efficient, and the proposed test for the null hypothesis of an Archimedean structure is consistent, asymptotically normal, and asymptotically optimal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a semiparametric procedure based on the empirical distribution function of a bivariate sample can be used to estimate the dependence structure between the two variates.
it is possible to obtain an estimator of a copula function which does not require the specification of the marginal distributions.
it is possible to estimate the dependence structure of two variates in the presence of an unknown marginal distribution function, without making any assumption on the dependence structure.
